newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan group to begin Sakhalin appraisal drilling.
newsitem.headline: Japan group to begin Sakhalin appraisal drilling.

text.p: Preliminary drilling is set to begin in the potentially giant oil and gas fields offshore Russia's far east island of Sakhalin, the Japanese consortium spearheading the $12 billion Sakhalin 1 project said on Tuesday.

"Drilling is scheduled to commence on July 16," said an official with the Sakhalin Oil and Gas Development Co Ltd (SODECO), which comprises the semi-governmental Japan National Oil Company and 13 other private Japanese companies.
A planning adviser with JNOC also said that a Wednesday start to drilling was likely.
"We are planning a total of three appraisal wells from two offshore rigs. Two of the wells will begin tomorrow, with a third drilled at a later date," the adviser said.
Drilling will continue until early October, while the region is clear of ice, he added.

The Sakhalin 1 project, whose three deposits are said to boast reserves of some 2.5 billion barrels of crude oil and over 15 trillion cubic feet of natural gas, is expected to begin full-scale production around 2001.
"We are expecting results from the drilling by the end of the summer and will take that and existing data to guide us toward full development with our partners," the JNOC adviser said.

The project, considered pivotal to Japan's future energy plans, had been hampered by delays caused by Russian red tape at the local level involving improper customs charges on exploration and drilling equipment.

But a June trip to Tokyo by First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov -- aimed at jump-starting the project by eliminating the tariffs -- was warmly received by Japan oil and gas companies and looks to have cleared the way toward full-fledged production.
